title: Early improvising on "Old Fashioned Love" and Erroll Garner
summary: Carter recalls improvising on Old Fashioned Love about 1921 and says Erroll Garner shows the mystery.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well, let me go back just to see if we can say something rather, about how is it that one learns to improvise?

I don't know. I think the first sound that I really remember learning and maybe improvising something on, of course, was something I didn't record until many years later, but it was a tune called "Old Fashioned Love" that -- and it seems to me that might have been about 1921 or thereabouts, "Old Fashioned Love", da doo dee da ... I think that was written by .. was it written by James Johnson?
I was gonna try him or Mel Stizel.
I would say him or Arthur ... not Arthur Briggs. Who wrote "Running Wild"?
Again, Mel Stizel seems to ring a bell.

NO. No. It was ... Arthur Briggs was the trumpet player in Paris --but there was another -- could there be 2 Arthur Briggs? I never thought of this before but he was ... Gibbs! Arthur Dr. Gibbs, I think, yeah, a pianist.
I think he wrote "Old Fashioned Love" or, maybe J.P. Johnson. I don't think Mel Stizel. No. I don't think so. But gee, when you say, how does one learn

to improvise ... you know who you should ask that of? Erroll Garner Earl Gunner. And you know why I say that, don't you? He hadn't had any formal training. He doesn't read music. He just sits down and plays what, you know, what comes to him. Now how do you -- go ahead.
You want me to tell you this, I know, as this is supposed to be my answer, but it kind of baffles me, too. How does one learn to improvise.
